title: Ghost Student
summary: Build a point, make it pickable, extract a reusable PointBody class in Lines, then record its positions in Trace. Full code and fresh native evidence accompany each state.

states.title: Build one point from scratch

brief.bring: An empty Node3D named PointStudy with a new point.gd script.
brief.make: One static point with a sphere surface and matching physical boundary.
brief.given: Day Zero supplies the room, camera or player, and lighting.
brief.build: Create the static body, sphere mesh and collision shape; use one radius and centre; attach both shapes beneath the point.
brief.check: One matching surface and boundary; radius and centre changes reach both; visibility and collision can change separately.
brief.later: Coordinates continues this exact script with pickup and a local/world readout.

states.provenance: Built from the complete printed Point One script on an empty Node3D. Every point object is created in this script; no material helper or reconstructed starting fixture is assumed. The saved native report tests this exact tutorial snapshot and code.
states.carry: The complete point.gd: one static body whose mesh and collider share a radius and centre.
states.nextStatus: Coordinates starts with these exact saved bytes and preserves this shape construction.

evidence.negativeControl: The saved report includes a deliberately broken point and records the expected failed checks. Expected failures: point_one/default/visible_sphere.

states.title: Carry the same point and read its position

brief.bring: The actual saved Point One point.gd and the same PointStudy node.
brief.make: The existing point can be carried and released, with its local and world positions shown.
brief.given: Configured XR hands, Godot XR Tools and the museum collision settings.
brief.build: Change StaticBody3D to XRToolsPickable, configure pickup before tree entry, and add a Label3D updated from global_position and to_local().
brief.check: Surface and collider follow together; release stays; the readout tracks the same point in the study and world frames.
brief.later: Lines continues this exact point and readout, adding a second endpoint, a segment and distance.

states.provenance: The complete printed Coordinates script continues the actual tested Point One output. Exact declared edits change the body type and settings and add a LOCAL/WORLD label; the existing mesh and collider construction is preserved. Native XR Tools pickup and release are exercised with synthetic controllers.
states.carry: The original point is pickable. Its surface and collider stay together, and a station-owned label reads local and world coordinates each frame.
states.nextStatus: Lines continues these exact saved bytes, retains the point and coordinate readout, and adds a second endpoint and live distance.

changes.after:
var point: XRToolsPickable
var readout: Label3D

changes.text:
point.freeze = true
    point.freeze_mode = RigidBody3D.FREEZE_MODE_KINEMATIC
    point.release_mode = XRToolsPickable.ReleaseMode.FROZEN
    point.ranged_grab_method = XRToolsPickable.RangedMethod.NONE
    point.collision_layer = 4
    point.collision_mask = 196615

readout = Label3D.new()
    readout.position = Vector3(0, 1.6, 0)
    readout.font_size = 36
    readout.pixel_size = 0.005
    add_child(readout)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
    var world_position := point.global_position
    var local_position := to_local(world_position)
    readout.text = "LOCAL " + str(local_position) + "\nWORLD " + str(world_position)

evidence.negativeControl: The saved report includes deliberately broken pickup/readout behavior and records the expected failed checks. Expected failures: point_coordinates/default/initial_readout, point_coordinates/default/held_readout, point_coordinates/default/released_readout, point_coordinates/default/changed_frame_readout, point_coordinates/default/moved_body_readout.

states.title: One point class, two instances

brief.bring: The tested Coordinates point.gd with its point, surface, collider and LOCAL/WORLD readout.
brief.make: Two held endpoints, a live segment, and the distance between them.
brief.given: Prepared unit-scale museum study, light/camera/XR hands and library; fully printed line_skin.gd renderer. PointBody is learner code.
brief.build: Move familiar geometry and pickup settings into PointBody._init; make A and B with .new; keep positions/readout/relation in the lesson. Convert both ends to local coordinates; subtract, measure and draw.
brief.check: Both instances inherit pickup, move and release independently. Editing one mesh/collider resource leaves the other alone. Segment/readout follow; parallel, +, X and depth exercises work.
brief.later: Trace stores positions in order. Grid will reuse points and relations without a pickup body at every position.

states.provenance: The complete printed script extracts the tested Coordinates construction into point_body.gd and creates two instances. The class construction is checked against the predecessor. Each point owns its mesh and collider; native XR pickup, resource independence and line relations are verified.
states.carry: PointBody class, two independent pickable instances, coordinate readout and live segment. Trace reuses the class unchanged.
states.nextStatus: Trace continues this exact script by keeping the original held point and recording accepted local positions. Grid remains planned.

changes.before:
point.freeze = true
    point.freeze_mode = RigidBody3D.FREEZE_MODE_KINEMATIC
    point.release_mode = XRToolsPickable.ReleaseMode.FROZEN
    point.ranged_grab_method = XRToolsPickable.RangedMethod.NONE
    point.collision_layer = 4
    point.collision_mask = 196615

    var surface := MeshInstance3D.new()
    var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
    sphere.radius = RADIUS
    sphere.height = RADIUS * 2.0
    surface.mesh = sphere
    point.add_child(surface)

    var boundary := CollisionShape3D.new()
    var shape := SphereShape3D.new()
    shape.radius = RADIUS
    boundary.shape = shape
    point.add_child(boundary)

changes.text:
var point_b: XRToolsPickable
var line: MeshInstance3D
var distance := 0.0

point_b = PointBody.new()
    point_b.position = CENTRE + Vector3(1.0, 0, 0)
    add_child(point_b)

    line = LineSkin.new()
    add_child(line)

var a := local_position
    var b := to_local(point_b.global_position)
    var displacement := b - a
    distance = displacement.length()
    line.show_segment(a, displacement, distance)
    readout.text += "\nDISTANCE " + str(distance)

evidence.negativeControl: Deliberate faults fail the same normal checks: shared resources, frozen segment, mixed frames.

states.title: The original point leaves a trace

brief.bring: The verified Lines program, learner PointBody class and supplied line renderer.
brief.make: One held point records an ordered sequence of positions, with visible segments joining adjacent samples.
brief.given: Prepared unit-scale museum study, light/camera/XR hands and library; fully printed line_skin.gd renderer. PointBody is learner code.
brief.build: Keep PointBody unchanged. Replace B/live span with a seeded Array[Vector3]; append when distance from last retained >= threshold; loop neighbouring entries to redraw. Keep history outside the point class.
brief.check: Stationary and short movement add no sample; enough accumulated movement does; stored positions remain ordered; the segment count follows the accepted positions; pickup and release still use the original point.
brief.later: Grid will reuse positions and relations. It has no assembled student state yet.

states.provenance: The complete printed Trace script continues the verified class-based Lines program. PointBody and LineSkin are carried byte for byte. The lesson owns the array, threshold and neighbour loop. This source-code continuation does not transfer a running museum session.
states.carry: Unchanged PointBody class, coordinate readout and a station-local position array separate from its segment drawing. The record lasts with this station; no Grid transfer yet.
states.nextStatus: Grid can build on stored positions and repeated relations. No Grid student code or native evidence has been assembled.
